title: SCIM: resilient user & group lifecycle orchestration with admin recovery flows
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customer SSO integrations (SAML/SCIM) surface intermittent failures and partial successes during bulk provisioning and deprovisioning. Current behavior: when a subset of group membership writes fail we log an error but surface limited remediation tools to admins. This ticket designs and implements a resilient orchestration layer for SCIM user/group lifecycle work with idempotent operations, tenant-aware backoff, audited dead-lettering, and an admin recovery UI. Goals:
- Make provisioning/deprovisioning idempotent and observable (correlate by externalId + request token).
- Implement exponential backoff + tenant jitter buckets to avoid noisy-tenant storms and adhere to downstream provider rate limits.
- Add a durable dead-letter queue (DLQ) for operations that exhaust retries, enriched with audit metadata and remediation instructions.
- Provide a console tool for admins to inspect, replay, or force-resolve DLQ items with clear RBAC gating and audit trails.
- Preserve a safe deprovision flow: quarantine window, tombstone marker, and automated reclaim after TTL unless admin explicitly purges.
Scope: SCIM v2 user and group endpoints, group-membership ops, bulk mode, and async retry controller. Not in scope: changes to SAML assertion parsing (covered in separate ticket).
Success metrics: reduce manual reconcile tickets by 70% for SSO customers, 99th-pct provisioning latency under new backoff SLO for successful reps, DLQ size <= 0.5% of daily ops after 2 weeks.
comments: 2025-11-13 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff notes - synced with PM (Clara) and Design (Jon). Agreed to prioritize idempotency and observable DLQs over complex transactional semantics across separate tenants.

2025-11-18 - Ravi Singh: Spike complete — implemented request-token idempotency in local mock and validated group-add semantics for repeated requests. Found a race when user creation and membership patch happen concurrently; added intentional sequencing with optimistic checks.
2025-11-21 - Design (Jon Lee): Console mockups uploaded — DLQ detail page + action buttons (Replay / Ignore / Force-delete). Link: https://confluence.redwood/team/identity/dlq-console-v1
2025-11-26 - PM (Clara Zhao): Prioritization update — P1, deliver minimal replay UX + API first, admin flow in console v1 for initial rollout. Added label 'admin-tools'.

2025-11-30 - Engineering review: PR feedback (GH: redwood/infra#2897) requests stronger telemetry (trace IDs on all SCIM ops) and a runbook entry. Action: add trace-id propagation and create initial runbook draft.

2025-12-02 - Security review: requested explicit RBAC check for DLQ actions (only admin+security roles can force-delete). Also require audit entries with operator identity on replay — flagged as security_review_required.

2025-12-03 - Ravi Singh: Implemented tenant backoff buckets and DLQ enrichment (added original payload, attempt count, last-error, trace-id). Running e2e tests against Okta sandbox — see job: https://ci.redwood/identity/12067/build/5
runbook: Add runbook entry: Investigate DLQ item -> review trace-id in traces -> check tenant backoff bucket state -> attempt replay with admin token -> mark resolved or escalate to SRE/SEC. Timeline: aim for <30min manual triage for P1 customers.
rollout_plan: API-first rollout: enable idempotency & retry controller behind feature flag for 10% of tenants for 48h, monitor DLQ rates and provisioning errors, then 100% rollout. Console replay disabled during initial 10% phase; enable after 48h if DLQ behavior is acceptable.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full two-phase commit across provider and Redwood is unsafe for multi-tenant scale; chose eventual-consistency with explicit tombstones + quarantine to avoid accidental data loss. We will provide atomicity at the operation level (create user, then idempotent add-to-group), and surface cross-op failures in DLQ for manual or automated remediation.
